title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractAnode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) offer a promising route to low cost, high-energy-density energy storage, but their practical application is limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here we report a molecular-level electrolyte design strategy that mitigates sodium loss by simultaneously promoting highly reversible sodium deposition and suppressing electrolyte decomposition, enabled by the cyclic ether 1,3-dioxane (DOX). Weak coordination of DOX with Na+ facilitates Na+ desolvation and reversible sodium deposition, while controlled DOX oligomerization forms a thin and robust solid–electrolyte interphase that suppresses continuous electrolyte decomposition and stabilizes sodium plating/stripping. As a result, 300-mAh-level AFSB pouch cells with a cathode loading of ~20 mg cm−2 retain ~80% capacity after 1,400 cycles at 1 C, operate at rates up to 3 C, maintain 88% capacity at −40 °C and achieve a round-trip energy efficiency up to ~98%. These results demonstrate a molecular electrolyte design strategy for extending the lifetime of AFSBs.
